_comment: Reference data for the knowledge base's memory model: how a re-observed fact or edge keeps its sighting history (tools/kb/knowledge_base.py), and how a new value in a single-valued slot is reconciled against the standing one by authority tier and effective date (tools/kb/kb_reconcile.py). Tunables only, never case data (RULE 1). Read through kb_refs.load_ref; a missing or broken file falls back to the pre-upgrade behaviour (newest evidence_ref only, nothing reconciled) with a stderr WARNING.

observations._comment: Sighting history on facts and edges. `evidence_refs_cap` = how many distinct evidence_refs (newest first) a record keeps as backing for its sightings; the single `evidence_ref` field always names the newest. Raising it costs only entity-file / fold-line size.

single_valued._comment: Attributes that hold ONE current value at a time, so a new, different value is reconciled (kb_reconcile.py: create / supersede / dispute / skip) instead of silently sitting beside the old one. Everything not listed stays multi-valued (nameservers, tech, trackers, previous_registrant_* eras …). Registrant LINKS are edges and are never reconciled — whois_eras.py already models a change of owner. Deliberately absent: `kind` (an indicator's type label), first_shown/last_shown (window bounds, kept as validity) and `display_name` (an org node keeps every registrar spelling; display_value picks one).

authority_order._comment: Authority tiers, LOWEST first. A new value supersedes a standing one only if its tier is >= the standing value's AND its effective date (valid_from, else first observation) is >= too; otherwise it is stored as disputed. Newer is never assumed truer, and a higher rank alone never wins. Exception: the SAME source+collector reporting a new value on the same or a later observation day updates its own claim (supersedes it). `analyst` = `attributes` rows on findings imported by tools/evidence_import.py, whatever the Admiralty grade.

authority_sources._comment: Tier by a record's `source`, checked FIRST — for sources whose collector is generic (ChongLuaDao and Webamon verdicts arrive through webpivot/pivot_extract). Unlisted sources fall through to authority_collectors.

authority_collectors._comment: Tier by a record's `collector` (exact match, then glob patterns). Registry = the WHOIS/RDAP parse and live DNS; vendor = indexed third-party corpora; extractor = what was read off a page, an archive capture or a binary; derived = the engine's own inferences.

authority_default._comment: Tier for a writer listed nowhere above. Extractor on purpose: an unknown collector can never silently override registry or analyst data.

abstract._comment: cases/<id>/abstract.json (tools/case_abstract.py) — the short per-case summary recall shows BEFORE any fact detail. `bluf_chars` caps the BLUF excerpt (its first sentence, ~50 tokens at 300); `max_domains` caps the cluster domains listed. Detail stays one step away in assessment.md / pipeline status.
